messages:
alex: Heads up — starting ~09:12 UTC we saw a spike of NCCL allreduce failures on eu-west GPU fleet (jobs A/B/C). Users report p99 latency doubling and intermittent task restarts. Logs show repeated 'ibv_exp_post_send: -110' followed by 'tx timeout, QP reset'.
sara: Which racks/nodes are affected? any pattern across ToRs?
alex: Roughly racks eu-west-3a: nodes g4-{12..18}, and eu-west-3b: g5-04. Stacktrace/snippet: ```[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] ERROR nccl: allreduce failed: -110 (ibv_exp_post_send)
[2026-03-15T09:12:34Z] WARN gpudirect: tx timeout qpn=0x2e5f
[2026-03-15T09:12:35Z] INFO kernel: mlx5_core 0000:84:00.0: mlx5e_wq_async_tx_timeout: tx timeout```
priya: Network side — I pulled counters on the leafs for those racks. Seeing a small but consistent increase in udp fragmentation and some rx errors on the MLX5 ports for those VLANs. Also noticed mismatch on MTU advertised between host and leaf when QinQ is enabled.
mateo: Could this be PFC or pause frame related? We've had issues where asymmetric pause handling + RoCEv2 UDP path causes retransmits.
priya: I dug deeper. On one affected host: `ip link show dev eth0 mtu 9000` but the ToR SVI has 9216 configured on the provider-vlan trunk. With QinQ double-tagging we effectively lose 4 bytes to tags on some paths; that causes occasional IP fragmentation for jumbo UDP frames used by RoCEv2.
sara: Ah — fragmentation on RoCEv2 is nasty, MR registration or GPUDirect can fail if packets are fragmented, leading to ibv errors. Any packet captures?
alex: Captured a short tcpdump on host and on leaf at same time: `tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 4791 -w /tmp/roce.pcap` showed large UDP frames with MF flag in one direction.
priya: Commands I ran: `ethtool -k eth0` -> GRO/TSO on; `bridge fdb show` -> some stale entries; `ip -s -d link show dev eth0` -> dropped align errors when VLAN tag mismatch occurred.
mateo: Quick mitigation: reduce MTU on hosts to 9000->8950 to avoid fragmentation through QinQ? Longer: fix SVI/trunk to consistent 9000 path MTU or remove double-tag on that tenant.
alex: Users need short-term fix. Proposal: 1) set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 for affected job queues to force TCP fallback (performance hit but stable) 2) apply host-level workaround: `ip link set dev eth0 mtu 8950` via k8s node daemonset 3) schedule network config change on ToRs to unify MTU and remove unintended QinQ for that tenant. Thoughts?
sara: +1 on the config path. For short term, I'd prefer host MTU change + disable GRO/TSO on NIC for those nodes too (`ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off`) — reduces chance of large fragmented packets.
priya: Will run a rolling change on the 10 affected nodes in eu-west-3a, can test with `ibv_rc_pingpong` and `ib_send_bw` before flipping. Also will gather MLX5 debug counters and dmesg before/after.
mateo: I'll coordinate with job-scheduler to set NCCL_IB_DISABLE on the small set of queues; need to warn users about perf regression.
engbot: deploy-bot: Scheduled daemonset rollout to set MTU=8950 on 2026-03-15T10:05Z (rd:infra-mtu-fix). Monitor window 30m.
alex: After the daemonset rollout + GRO/TSO off on a canary node: observed mtu-consistent packets and no more ibv errors in that canary run (short test). Pushing the host MTU/GRO change to the rest now.
sara: Good. Follow-up actions: - Network: schedule ToR trunk/SVI MTU homogenization and remove accidental QinQ for tenant X (priority high) - Infra: keep GRO/TSO off on these nodes until network fix done - Runtime: collect perf delta for NCCL_IB_DISABLE vs default and document fallback cost - Postmortem: include pcap and config diffs
priya: I'll attach pcaps and MLX5 counters to the incident ticket after rollout.
mateo: I'll update the docs about RDMA path MTU requirements and add a preflight check to infra provisioning that verifies host, leaf, and trunk MTU match when enabling RoCE.
alex: Thanks everyone. If anyone sees reoccurrence after full roll, ping this thread. :thumbsup:
